operationalLogic: The Onewheel GT S-Series operates as a self-balancing, single-wheeled electric skateboard. Rider presence and intent are detected by pressure sensors embedded in the footpads. An onboard Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) continuously monitors the board's pitch, roll, and angular velocity. This data, combined with rider input, is processed by the Electronic Speed Controller (ESC), which precisely controls the brushless hub motor. By leaning forward or backward, the rider causes a change in the board's pitch, which the ESC counters by adjusting the motor's speed and direction, maintaining balance and providing propulsion. The motor actively drives the wheel to keep the board level and the rider upright, functioning as a stabilized inverted pendulum system. Regenerative braking is engaged by leaning back, converting kinetic energy into electrical energy to recharge the battery.
